user.title: Connect to pveupdate
user.description: Run `pveupdate serve` on your Proxmox host and get the token with `pveupdate token`.

reauth_confirm.title: New pveupdate token
reauth_confirm.description: The token was rejected, or the host's certificate no longer matches it. Get the current one on the host with `pveupdate token`.

reconfigure.title: New pveupdate token
reconfigure.description: Get the current token on the host with `pveupdate token`. With pveupdate 0.8.0 or later it also moves the connection to HTTPS.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach pveupdate on that host and port. Is `pveupdate serve` running? After updating pveupdate, restart it with `systemctl restart pveupdate-serve`.

abort.already_configured: This host is already set up.

insecure_http.title: pveupdate connection to {host} is not encrypted
insecure_http.description: Home Assistant sends the token for {host} over plain HTTP, so it can be read on your network. Update pveupdate on the host to 0.8.0 or later, run `systemctl restart pveupdate-serve` and `pveupdate token`, then paste the result under the integration's Reconfigure.

init.title: Proxmox Guest Updates options
init.description: Choose the LXCs and VMs pveupdate manages. Untracked guests are removed from Home Assistant.

error.cannot_list_guests: Could not get the guest list from pveupdate. Update pveupdate on the host to 0.6.0 or later, and check `pveupdate serve` is running.
error.guests_locked: Tracked guests can only be changed on the host, because `remote-track` is off there. You can still change the check interval.
error.busy: A check or update is running. Try again when it finishes.
